title: Grade 7 Science — Mon, May 18
description: Nutrition in Animals — Day 1 of 5: Modes of feeding
subject: science

questions.question: Why do animals need food?
options: For energy, growth, and repair of body
questions.explanation: Animals need food for energy (to move, breathe), growth, repair of worn-out cells, and to fight diseases.

questions.question: Animals that eat only plants are called:
questions.explanation: Herbivores (herba = plant) eat only plants. Examples: cow, horse, rabbit, deer.

questions.question: Animals that eat only other animals are called:
questions.explanation: Carnivores eat only animal flesh. Examples: lion, tiger, eagle, shark.

questions.question: Animals that eat both plants and animals are called:
questions.explanation: Omnivores eat both plants and animals. Examples: humans, bear, crow, dog.

questions.question: Which of these is a carnivore?
questions.explanation: Lion eats only meat (other animals) — it is a carnivore.

questions.question: What is digestion?
options: The absorption of food into blood
The breakdown of complex food into simpler, absorbable substances
The removal of waste from the body
questions.explanation: Digestion is the process of breaking down complex food molecules (like starch) into simpler forms (like glucose) that the body can absorb.

questions.question: The human digestive system begins at the:
questions.explanation: Digestion begins in the mouth where food is chewed (mechanical digestion) and mixed with saliva (chemical digestion).

questions.question: Which enzyme in saliva starts the digestion of starch?
questions.explanation: Salivary amylase in saliva begins the digestion of starch (carbohydrates) in the mouth.

questions.question: The long tube through which food moves from mouth to stomach is:
questions.explanation: The oesophagus (food pipe) connects the mouth to the stomach. Food moves through it by a wave-like motion called peristalsis.

questions.question: Digestion of proteins mainly occurs in the:
questions.explanation: The stomach produces pepsin (acid enzyme) and hydrochloric acid which break down proteins.

questions.question: Which organ produces bile to digest fats?
questions.explanation: The liver produces bile, which is stored in the gall bladder and released into the small intestine to break down (emulsify) fats.

questions.question: Where does most digestion and absorption of nutrients happen?
questions.explanation: The small intestine is the main site of both digestion and absorption. Its inner surface has villi that increase surface area.

questions.question: The main function of the large intestine is:
questions.explanation: The large intestine absorbs excess water from undigested food and compacts the remaining material into faeces.

questions.question: Amoeba feeds by:
questions.explanation: Amoeba engulfs food particles by extending finger-like projections called pseudopodia, forming a food vacuole.

questions.question: Finger-like projections in the small intestine that increase surface area are called:
questions.explanation: Villi (singular: villus) are tiny finger-like projections on the inner wall of the small intestine that increase surface area for absorption.
